title: Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026

claims.claim: This bill rewrites two bankruptcy debt-limit rules in title 11 of the U.S. Code.
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 2. DEBT LIMIT MODIFICATIONS

claims.claim: It replaces the current definition of "debtor" in Section 1182(1).
claims.sourceSpan: Section 1182(1) of title 11, United States Code, is amended to read as follows

claims.claim: Section 1182(1) is the eligibility gate for Subchapter V small business reorganization under Chapter 11.
claims.sourceSpan: SUBCHAPTER V - SMALL BUSINESS DEBTOR REORGANIZATION

claims.claim: The new definition covers a person engaged in commercial or business activities.
claims.sourceSpan: person engaged in commercial or business activities

claims.claim: Affiliates are counted together (any affiliate that is also a debtor).
claims.sourceSpan: including any affiliate of such person that is also a debtor under this title

claims.claim: Single-asset real estate is excluded.
claims.sourceSpan: excluding a person whose primary activity is the business of owning single asset real estate

claims.claim: It has aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts of not more than $7.5M.
claims.sourceSpan: aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts as of the date of the filing of the petition or the date of the order for relief in an amount not more than $7,500,000 (excluding debts owed to 1 or more affiliates or insiders) not less than 50 percent of which arose from the commercial or business activities of the debtor

claims.claim: Debt owed to affiliates or insiders is excluded from the $7.5M total.
claims.sourceSpan: excluding debts owed to 1 or more affiliates or insiders

claims.claim: At least 50 percent of the debt arose from commercial or business activities.
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 50 percent of which arose from the commercial or business activities of the debtor

claims.claim: It bars public reporting companies and their affiliates from Subchapter V.
claims.sourceSpan: any debtor that is a corporation subject to the reporting requirements under section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m, 78o(d))

claims.claim: It disallows any group of affiliated debtors whose combined qualifying debts exceed $7.5M.
claims.sourceSpan: any member of a group of affiliated debtors under this title that has aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts in an amount greater than $7,500,000
claims.note: Source excludes any MEMBER of such a group; the summary compresses this to 'any group.' Same practical effect on the group; the top_lines/sections/underreported fields all state 'any member' correctly. Minor imprecision, not material.

claims.claim: Second, it rewrites Section 109(e).
claims.sourceSpan: Section 109 of title 11, United States Code is amended by striking subsection (e) and inserting the following

claims.claim: Only individuals with regular income (or such an individual and spouse, other than a stockbroker or commodity broker) qualify under the new Chapter 13 rule.
claims.sourceSpan: an individual with regular income and such individual's spouse, except a stockbroker or a commodity broker

claims.claim: Noncontingent liquidated debts must aggregate less than $2.75M to be eligible to file under Chapter 13.
claims.sourceSpan: noncontingent, liquidated debts that aggregate less than $2,750,000

claims.claim: This replaces the current split limits for secured and unsecured debt.
claims.sourceSpan: noncontingent, liquidated, unsecured debts of less than $250,000

claims.claim: The amendments apply to cases commenced on or after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: The amendments made by this Act shall apply to any case that is commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Rewrites Subchapter V small business bankruptcy eligibility to a single $7.5M combined-debt limit.
claims.sourceSpan: in an amount not more than $7,500,000

claims.claim: Rewrites Chapter 13 individual eligibility to a single $2.75M combined-debt limit.
claims.sourceSpan: noncontingent, liquidated debts that aggregate less than $2,750,000

claims.claim: Effective for cases filed on or after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any case that is commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Headline: Subchapter V Small Business Debt Limit (billSection 2(a)).
claims.sourceSpan: Modification to the Small Business Bankruptcy Debt Limit

claims.claim: New 11 U.S.C. §1182(1)(A) covers persons engaged in commercial/business activities (including affiliates that are also debtors) with aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts of not more than $7.5M (excluding debt owed to affiliates or insiders).
claims.sourceSpan: aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts as of the date of the filing of the petition or the date of the order for relief in an amount not more than $7,500,000 (excluding debts owed to 1 or more affiliates or insiders) not less than 50 percent of which arose from the commercial or business activities of the debtor

claims.claim: At least 50 percent of the debt must have arisen from the commercial or business activities of the debtor.
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 50 percent of which arose from the commercial or business activities of the debtor

claims.claim: Excludes single-asset real estate debtors whose primary activity is owning single-asset real estate.
claims.sourceSpan: excluding a person whose primary activity is the business of owning single asset real estate

claims.claim: Headline: Subchapter V Group and Public-Company Exclusions (billSection 2(a)).
claims.sourceSpan: does not include

claims.claim: Bars any member of a group of affiliated debtors whose aggregate qualifying debts exceed $7.5M (excluding debt owed to affiliates or insiders).
claims.sourceSpan: any member of a group of affiliated debtors under this title that has aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts in an amount greater than $7,500,000

claims.claim: Bars any debtor that is a corporation subject to Section 13 or 15(d) reporting under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m, 78o(d)).
claims.sourceSpan: any debtor that is a corporation subject to the reporting requirements under section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m, 78o(d))

claims.claim: Bars any debtor that is an affiliate of such a public reporting company.
claims.sourceSpan: any debtor that is an affiliate of a corporation described in clause (ii)

claims.claim: Headline: Chapter 13 Individual Debt Limit (billSection 2(b)).
claims.sourceSpan: Modification to the Consumer Bankruptcy Debt Limit

claims.claim: New 11 U.S.C. §109(e): only an individual with regular income (or such an individual and spouse, other than a stockbroker or commodity broker) with noncontingent, liquidated debts that aggregate less than $2.75M is eligible to file under Chapter 13.
claims.sourceSpan: Only an individual with regular income that owes, on the date of the filing of the petition, noncontingent, liquidated debts that aggregate less than $2,750,000

claims.claim: Replaces the current version of §109(e), which splits its debt limit into a secured-debt cap and an unsecured-debt cap.
claims.sourceSpan: noncontingent, liquidated, secured debts of less than $750,000

claims.claim: Headline: Effective Date (billSection 3).
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 3. EFFECTIVE DATE

claims.claim: The amendments made by the Act apply to any case commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: The amendments made by this Act shall apply to any case that is commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Rewrites the definition of "debtor" for Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (Small Business Debtor Reorganization).
claims.sourceSpan: SUBCHAPTER V - SMALL BUSINESS DEBTOR REORGANIZATION

claims.claim: Subparagraph (A) covers a person engaged in commercial or business activities (including any affiliate that is also a debtor, excluding single-asset real estate) with aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts, as of filing/order for relief, of not more than $7.5M (excluding debts to affiliates/insiders), not less than 50% arising from commercial/business activities.
claims.sourceSpan: aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts as of the date of the filing of the petition or the date of the order for relief in an amount not more than $7,500,000 (excluding debts owed to 1 or more affiliates or insiders) not less than 50 percent of which arose from the commercial or business activities of the debtor

claims.claim: Adds three Subchapter V exclusions in new §1182(1)(B).
claims.sourceSpan: does not include

claims.claim: Excludes: (i) any member of an affiliated-debtor group with aggregate debts greater than $7.5M (excluding debt to affiliates/insiders); (ii) any corporation subject to §13 or §15(d) reporting under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. §78m, §78o(d)); (iii) any affiliate of a corporation in clause (ii).
claims.sourceSpan: any member of a group of affiliated debtors under this title that has aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts in an amount greater than $7,500,000

claims.claim: Strikes and rewrites §109(e) so Chapter 13 eligibility is set by a single combined-debt cap.
claims.sourceSpan: amended by striking subsection (e) and inserting the following

claims.claim: New §109(e): an individual with regular income (or such individual and spouse, except a stockbroker/commodity broker) with noncontingent, liquidated debts aggregating less than $2.75M may be a Chapter 13 debtor; per the fetched current §109 this replaces a split secured/unsecured cap with a single aggregate threshold.
claims.sourceSpan: an individual with regular income and such individual's spouse, except a stockbroker or a commodity broker, that owe, on the date of the filing of the petition, noncontingent, liquidated debts that aggregate less than $2,750,000

claims.claim: Applies the amendments to any case commenced under title 11 on or after the date of enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any case that is commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Pending cases filed before enactment remain governed by prior law.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any case that is commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment of this Act
claims.note: Logical entailment of the effective-date clause (cases commenced before enactment fall outside the amendment's scope, so prior law governs); correct but not stated verbatim in source.

claims.claim: The affiliated-group cap treats any member of an affiliated-debtor group whose combined qualifying debts exceed $7.5M as ineligible for Subchapter V, even if that member alone would qualify.
claims.sourceSpan: any member of a group of affiliated debtors under this title that has aggregate noncontingent liquidated secured and unsecured debts in an amount greater than $7,500,000
claims.note: Group-aggregate reading matches source; 'even if that member alone would qualify' is a correct inference from the aggregate test, not stated verbatim.

claims.claim: Coverage of Subchapter V threshold bills tends to focus on the headline dollar limit; the affiliated-group aggregation rule is the operative provision for holding-company/franchisee structures.
claims.note: Editorial rationale about coverage tendencies; not a bill-text claim. Non-fidelity meta-commentary.

claims.claim: Public reporting companies (§13 or §15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act) and their affiliates are barred from Subchapter V.
claims.sourceSpan: any debtor that is a corporation subject to the reporting requirements under section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m, 78o(d))

claims.claim: Subchapter V is generally understood to be for small businesses; codifying a categorical exclusion for reporting companies and affiliates closes a workaround for public-company subsidiaries.
claims.note: Editorial rationale; not a bill-text claim.

claims.claim: Sets a $7.5M Subchapter V cap and a $2.75M Chapter 13 cap but does not index either threshold to inflation, so real-terms limits will erode over time.
claims.sourceSpan: in an amount not more than $7,500,000
claims.note: Figures sourced; the bill text contains no inflation-indexing clause (verifiable by absence). NOTE: title 11 §104 provides periodic Judicial-Conference dollar-amount adjustment for §109(e) amounts (see ref usc-11-109 'Adjustment of Dollar Amounts'), so the erosion projection is analytical, not a source statement; the literal 'the bill does not index' is true. Not material.

claims.claim: Excludes public reporting companies and their affiliates from Subchapter V but does not address privately-held companies whose beneficial owners are public reporting entities.
claims.sourceSpan: any debtor that is an affiliate of a corporation described in clause (ii)
claims.note: Exclusion sourced; the 'privately-held beneficial-owner' gap is an analytical observation by absence.

claims.claim: Replaces the split secured/unsecured Chapter 13 debt limit with a single aggregate cap but does not address how debts secured by a spouse's separate property are counted.
claims.sourceSpan: noncontingent, liquidated debts that aggregate less than $2,750,000
claims.note: Single-cap sourced; spouse-separate-property gap is analytical by absence.

claims.claim: Applies only to cases commenced on or after enactment and does not offer transition relief for cases already dismissed on eligibility grounds under the prior thresholds.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any case that is commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of enactment of this Act
claims.note: Effective-date sourced; no-transition-relief gap is analytical by absence.

claims.claim: New categorical exclusions from Subchapter V for members of affiliated-debtor groups over $7.5M, public reporting companies under §13 or §15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and affiliates of such reporting companies (new §1182(1)(B)).
claims.sourceSpan: any debtor that is a corporation subject to the reporting requirements under section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78m, 78o(d))

claims.claim: 11 U.S.C. §1182(1) — Definition of "debtor" for Subchapter V rewritten to a $7.5M combined-debt cap with a 50%-commercial-origin requirement.
claims.sourceSpan: in an amount not more than $7,500,000 (excluding debts owed to 1 or more affiliates or insiders) not less than 50 percent

claims.claim: 11 U.S.C. §109(e) — Chapter 13 eligibility rewritten to a single $2.75M aggregate noncontingent-liquidated-debt cap.
claims.sourceSpan: noncontingent, liquidated debts that aggregate less than $2,750,000

notes: Source = S.3977 Engrossed in Senate (3024 chars) + referenced statutes usc-11-1182 (current §1182(1) = 'means a small business debtor') and usc-11-109 (current §109(e) = split $250,000 unsecured / $750,000 secured caps). All figures ($7,500,000, $2,750,000, 50 percent) verbatim in source; both dollar caps correctly bound to their accounts (Subchapter V/§1182(1) vs Chapter 13/§109(e)); no direction inversions; source fully covered (no material omissions). Only non-fidelity items: soft 'low-controversy' framing and editorial why_unreported rationale (minor/style debt); summary compresses 'any member of a group' to 'any group' (minor, stated correctly elsewhere).
